Operating Characteristics of the U-BOIN Design Across Scenarios

Source: R/sim_uboin_multi.R
sim_uboin_multi.Rd

Run sim_uboin under several scenarios of true DLT and response probabilities with the same design, and collect the main operating characteristics of every scenario in one table.

Usage

sim_uboin_multi(
  tox_upper,
  resp_lower,
  scenarios,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  target = NULL,
  resp_assoc = 0,
  utility = c(0, 30, 50, 100),
  n_stage1 = 12,
  n_stop = NULL,
  start_dose = 1,
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  prior_tox = c(1, 1),
  prior_resp = c(1, 1),
  keep_trials = FALSE,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

tox_upper

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, for example 0.30.

resp_lower

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, for example 0.20.

scenarios

List of scenarios, each a list with elements p_true and p_resp and optionally name. Names of the list are used as scenario names. All scenarios must have the same number of doses.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial; the maximum sample size is n_cohort * cohort_size.

cohort_size

Integer scalar. Number of patients per cohort.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

target

Numeric scalar or NULL. Target DLT probability of the BOIN design in stage I. Defaults to NULL, which uses tox_upper - 0.05.

resp_assoc

Numeric scalar. Association parameter of the Gumbel model that joins the DLT and the response of a patient; 0 makes them independent. Defaults to 0.

utility

Numeric vector of length four. Utility of the four outcomes, in the order of p_outcome. Defaults to c(0, 30, 50, 100), example 1 of the article.

n_stage1

Integer scalar. Stage II starts once a dose has this many patients (s1 of the article). Defaults to 12.

n_stop

Integer scalar or NULL. The trial ends once a dose has this many patients (s2 of the article). Defaults to NULL, the maximum sample size.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level of the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

p_saf

Numeric scalar. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic, for the boundaries of stage I. Defaults to 0.6 * target.

p_tox

Numeric scalar. Lowest DLT probability deemed overly toxic, for the boundaries of stage I. Defaults to 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is toxic when the posterior probability that its DLT probability exceeds tox_upper is above this value. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is futile when the posterior probability that its response probability is below resp_lower is above this value. Defaults to 0.90.

prior_tox

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the DLT probability in the toxicity rule, which eliminates doses in stage I as well as in stage II. Defaults to c(1, 1), the uniform prior of the BOIN design that stage I of the article uses.

prior_resp

Numeric vector of length two. Beta prior of the response probability in the futility rule. Defaults to c(1, 1).

keep_trials

Logical scalar. Keep the trial by trial data in the result of every scenario. Defaults to FALSE.

verbose

Logical scalar. Report progress while the simulation runs. Defaults to FALSE.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class uboin_oc_multi, which is a list with components

results

Named list of uboin_oc objects, one per scenario.

summary_table

Data frame with the true rates, the selection percentages and the average numbers of patients, DLTs and responses of every scenario and dose.

scenario_names

Character vector of scenario names.

n_doses

Number of doses.

call

The matched call.

Details

Every scenario is simulated with the same seed, so that the scenarios differ by their probabilities and not by the random numbers. The outcome probabilities of a scenario are given by its marginal rates and resp_assoc; to give them directly, run sim_uboin with p_outcome for each scenario.

References

Zhou, Y., Lee, J. J. and Yuan, Y. (2019). A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval (U-BOIN) phase I/II design to identify the optimal biological dose for targeted and immune therapies. Statistics in Medicine, 38(28), S5299-S5316. doi:10.1002/sim.8361

See also

sim_uboin

Examples

scenarios <- list(
  "Scenario 1" = list(p_true = c(0.02, 0.15, 0.30, 0.45, 0.60),
                      p_resp = c(0.20, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65, 0.65)),
  "Scenario 3" = list(p_true = c(0.05, 0.15, 0.30, 0.45, 0.60),
                      p_resp = c(0.08, 0.46, 0.25, 0.20, 0.10))
)

oc <- sim_uboin_multi(
  tox_upper = 0.30,
  resp_lower = 0.20,
  scenarios = scenarios,
  n_cohort = 18,
  cohort_size = 3,
  resp_assoc = 0.2,
  n_trials = 200,
  seed = 123
)
oc
